title: Wednesday’s holiday leftovers have a different deadline from Thursday’s turkey

paragraphs.text: Good Shepherd serves its community dinner Wednesday evening in Pontotoc. If you take a plate home from a holiday meal, ask when it was cooked. For food cooked Wednesday, Nov. 25, and promptly refrigerated, Sunday, Nov. 29, marks four days. For Thursday’s turkey, that point comes Monday, Nov. 30. Eat or freeze the leftovers within that window.

Start with the time the food spent on the table. USDA says to refrigerate perishable leftovers within two hours. Cut turkey off the bone and divide large quantities among shallow, covered containers. Store the meat separately from stuffing and gravy so it can chill quickly. Keep the refrigerator at 40°F or colder.

If you already know you will have more than the family can eat by the weekend, freeze part of the meal now. Mississippi State Extension recommends sealed containers and says frozen leftovers have the best flavor and texture within three to four months. Labeling a container with the day the meal was cooked makes it easier to keep Wednesday’s food separate from Thursday’s.

When you reheat a portion, use a food thermometer to check that it reaches 165°F. Bring soups, sauces and gravy to a boil. If a perishable dish has already sat at room temperature for more than two hours, discard it.
